title: Backend dispatch: from a feature to the code that computes it
alt: A requested feature runs on the device twin of the chosen backend when one fits, else on the CPU with its best SIMD path.
text: Runs on: GPU twin (CUDA, SYCL, HIP or Metal), CPU extractor (AVX-512, AVX2, NEON, SVE2 or scalar C).
Boxes: Options (--backend, --model, --feature), Features to compute (named by the model or the CLI), Extractor registry (by feature name and backend flag), Device twin? (provided_features, geometry).
Options → Features to compute → Extractor registry (vmaf_use_feature) → Device twin? → GPU twin (twin fits).

Scenario 1, GPU twin: With a GPU backend compiled in and allowed, a feature with a twin runs on the device. The model names its features; --backend cuda allows CUDA. Each feature is looked up in the registry. The CPU extractor names a CUDA twin through provided_features. The twin accepts the frame geometry and options, so it runs.

Scenario 2, CPU: Without a fitting twin, the CPU extractor runs its best SIMD path. --backend cpu, or no GPU backend compiled in. The feature is looked up. No twin is eligible. The CPU extractor runs; vmaf_init_cpu picked AVX-512, AVX2, NEON or scalar C.
Disabled backends (--no_cuda, --no_sycl, ...) leave the candidate list first.
With --backend NAME a missing or failing backend is an error, never a silent fall back to the CPU.
